summary: In this story, two friends calmly investigate a mysterious banging sound coming from an empty classroom and discover it is only a loose window shutter in the wind.
introduce: Act out a short mime, such as checking your watch and tapping your foot, and ask students how you feel and how they know. Explain that in “The Secret of the Empty Classroom” they will use clues in the same way to work out what the writer does not say directly.

keyTerms.def: to look closely into something in order to find out the truth
a reason or description that makes something clear
strange and difficult to explain or understand

challengeTerms.def: facts or signs that help show what is true
an idea that you test to see whether it is true
not easily convinced; wanting proof before believing something

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that if something sounds mysterious or scary, the best thing to do is stay away and never try to find out why? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how Omar and Lina investigate the mysterious sound instead of just believing the rumor.
struggling: Pre-teach investigate, explanation, and mysterious with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use evidence, hypothesis, and skeptical in a short paragraph that makes an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
